priorStories.headline: U.S.-China trade truce extended to January
priorStories.body:
China confirmed that its trade truce with the United States has been extended for two months, through January 10.

The countries also agreed to reduce tariffs on $60 billion in bilateral trade, divided evenly between lists of American and Chinese goods. No timetable for putting those reductions into effect was reported.

priorStories.headline: Myanmar airstrike reportedly kills at least 49
priorStories.body:
At least 49 people were killed and 58 wounded in an airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw, according to the Arakan Army and a rescue official. Twenty-two of the wounded were reported in critical condition.

The Arakan Army said a military jet dropped two bombs around noon. The Associated Press could not independently confirm the account, and Myanmar’s military had not commented.

priorStories.headline: Pennsylvania measles outbreak passes 900 cases
priorStories.body:
Pennsylvania recorded 68 additional measles infections since September 23, bringing the state’s outbreak total to 903.

Hospitalizations rose from 164 to 176, according to state health department data. Lancaster County remained the hardest-hit part of the state.

priorStories.headline: U.S. lowers 2031 vehicle fuel-economy standard
priorStories.body:
The Transportation Department finalized standards requiring automakers’ fleets to average 34.9 miles per gallon by 2031. The rule replaces a requirement of 50.4 mpg.

The department estimates that the lower standard will reduce manufacturers’ compliance costs but increase gasoline consumption and drivers’ lifetime fuel costs compared with the superseded rule.

priorStories.headline: Judge blocks election conditions on security grants
priorStories.body:
A federal judge blocked the Trump administration from withholding portions of federal counterterrorism grants unless state and local governments adopted election procedures backed by the administration.

U.S. District Judge Amir Ali ruled that Congress had not authorized the grant programs to be conditioned on those election-administration changes.

candidates.summary: Malaysia began returning 1,476 Myanmar nationals, including children, in the first phase of a program that could repatriate 5,000 people. Malaysia described the returns as voluntary. The U.N. refugee agency and rights groups raised safety concerns because of Myanmar’s civil war and questioned whether refugees and asylum-seekers were adequately protected.
candidates.title: Malaysia begins returning 1,476 Myanmar nationals

candidates.summary: Former special counsel Jack Smith told the Senate Judiciary Committee that he stood behind the federal criminal cases he brought against President Donald Trump and said his decisions were made without regard to politics. Republican senators accused Smith of partisan and improper investigative conduct, while Democratic senators defended the prosecutions.
candidates.title: Jack Smith defends Trump prosecutions at Senate hearing

candidates.summary: The U.S. government launched America.gov, an AI-based interface intended to help users find federal information and services. The site says its chatbot searches official government sources and provides citations, but does not identify the specific AI model it uses. It is free, has no advertising and does not require users to log in.
candidates.title: U.S. launches AI-based America.gov portal

candidates.summary: The Conference Board's U.S. consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September from 88.6 in August. Its measure of consumers' current conditions declined to 109.3, while the short-term expectations measure fell to 63.6.
candidates.title: U.S. consumer confidence falls in September

candidates.summary: Iran's currency reached a record low, with traders in Tehran exchanging more than 2.5 million rials per U.S. dollar. The previous reported low was 2.2 million rials per dollar on September 2. The decline came amid war, sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade affecting Iranian oil.
candidates.title: Iranian rial falls to record low

candidates.summary: Morocco's King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as head of government and tasked her with forming a cabinet after her Authenticity and Modernity Party won the most seats in the September 23 legislative election. Mansouri, previously urban planning minister and mayor of Marrakech, is the first woman appointed to lead Morocco's government.
candidates.title: Morocco appoints first woman head of government

sources.name: Embassy of Morocco in the United States

candidates.summary: The Premier League said an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges involving serious financial-rule breaches over nine seasons and most charges concerning failure to cooperate with the league's investigation. The commission found that the club used arrangements to inflate revenue and reduce reported costs. Sanctions will be decided separately, and Manchester City said it would pursue available appeals.
candidates.title: Manchester City found guilty of financial-rule breaches

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said leaders of major technology companies signed a voluntary artificial-intelligence accord providing for internal and external reviews. He described the agreement as morally binding and said the industry should largely police itself. Details of the accord, including its signatories, review standards and enforcement arrangements, were not immediately released.
candidates.title: Trump announces voluntary AI industry accord

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court temporarily lifted lower-court requirements that people facing deportation to countries other than their own receive an opportunity to object before removal. The apparent 6-3 order allows the administration's expedited third-country deportation policy to continue while the court considers its legality. Arguments are scheduled for December; the order did not decide the policy's ultimate lawfulness.
candidates.title: Supreme Court permits third-country deportations pending review

sources.name: Supreme Court of the United States

candidates.summary: OpenAI introduced proactive agents called Dots, designed to perform continuing tasks on users' behalf, and released GPT-6.1 Sol and a premium processing tier called Ultrafast. The announcements followed the company's decision a day earlier to halt another model's rollout because of security concerns. OpenAI said GPT-6.1 Sol is classified under its framework as Critical for cybersecurity capability and High for biological and chemical capability and uses its existing safeguards stack.
candidates.title: OpenAI introduces Dots agents and GPT-6.1 Sol

candidates.summary: The United States withdrew from the Council of Europe's Group of States against Corruption, known as GRECO. The Council of Europe said the U.S. formally notified it on September 28. The State Department confirmed the withdrawal and said participation did not provide tangible national-security benefits; GRECO said it remained open to renewed cooperation.
candidates.title: United States withdraws from European anti-corruption group
